_sources.discrepancies: NCSL classifies CT as 'non-photo ID requested' (voters without ID may sign an affidavit). Connecticut enacted no-excuse absentee voting in 2023 via constitutional amendment. Early in-person voting was also added beginning with the 2024 election cycle. Registration deadline is 7 days before the election per CT law (online/mail); same-day registration available at polls. 2026-06-10: Primary confirmed as August 11, 2026 with early voting August 3–9 per the Secretary of the State's office; general early voting runs October 19 – November 1, 2026.

earlyVoting.notes: Seven days of early voting for the August 11 primary: August 3–9, 2026. Hours are 10 a.m.–6 p.m. on Aug 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9, and 8 a.m.–8 p.m. on Aug 4 and 6. Locations vary by municipality.
Early in-person voting for the November 3 general election runs October 19 – November 1, 2026 (14 days, ending the second day before Election Day). Hours and locations vary by municipality.
Connecticut offers early in-person voting (14 days before a general election, 7 days before a primary). No-excuse absentee (mail) voting is also available. Hours and locations vary by municipality.

acceptedIds: Any document showing name and address (utility bill, bank statement, etc.)
Non-photo ID is requested for first-time voters who registered by mail and did not provide ID at registration
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Connecticut does not have a statewide ban on phones in polling places. Voters should not interfere with others or photograph ballots. Electioneering is prohibited within 75 feet of a polling place.
additionalRules: No-excuse absentee voting enacted via constitutional amendment, effective 2023. Any registered voter may request a mail ballot.
Closed primary: only voters registered with a party may vote in that party's primary. Unregistered or independent voters may not participate in partisan primaries.
Same-day voter registration available at polls with proof of identity and Connecticut residency.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason (no-excuse absentee, enacted 2023)
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Ballot request must be received by town clerk by 1 day before election; applications submitted in person by noon the day before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the town clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the town clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Connecticut has a closed primary (Conn. Gen. Stat. §9-395). Only voters registered with a political party may vote in that party's primary. Unaffiliated voters may not participate in a partisan primary unless they register with a party before the enrollment deadline (typically 7 days before the primary).
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Connecticut tiene una primaria cerrada (Conn. Gen. Stat. §9-395). Solo los votantes registrados en un partido político pueden votar en la primaria de ese partido. Los votantes sin afiliación no pueden participar en una primaria partidista a menos que se registren con un partido antes de la fecha límite de inscripción (generalmente 7 días antes de la primaria).
